p3c1.caption: STA W-I · 13,695 words · FIG GUN
p3c1.contentRationale: The suicide-that-isn't: gun to the temple lowered for a gray death; glass-cage bedroom; day-in-the-empire (blue-pencil slashes, Springville call, Gallstone plugging suppressed, board, Stoneridge maps, Toohey's Keating/Mrs.-Keating pitch, diamond-bracelet dismissal); forced life review (Hell's Kitchen daybreak raid, ferry-rail bootblack, betrayal of Mulligan, Banner rise, breaking men of integrity incl. Dwight Carson, locked gallery); closes on Toohey's crate — Mallory's statue — and the sculptor question.
p3c1.notes: CLIMAX-CLASS: solid Gilt numeral + full hearth. Muzzle-ring vignette (concentric Ash circles, Ember-deep bore); gray-death ring vs red bore. Verified: 'GAIL WYNAND RAISED A GUN TO HIS TEMPLE.' / 'yours, Gail Wynand, will be a gray death'.

p3c1.readingTreatment: Shared calm body; long-chapter relief (259 paras): asterism section rests; margin note 'the desire to desire'; Ember ◆ end-mark + END · FIG GUN

p3c2.caption: STA W-II · 5,953 words · FIG BRACELET
p3c2.contentRationale: The dead Keating marriage performing life before a fire after the Knowlton tea: parroted Gallstone review, country-house interrogation exposing borrowed motives, Keating's 'I' accusation turned back ('Where's yours, Peter?'), kneeling plea; Toohey engineers the Wynand meeting and toasts the Banner.
p3c2.notes: COLD: Bronze stroke numeral + Bronze end-mark. Emerald-bracelet arc + lamplight glint; toast-stem second detail. No drop-cap letterform (no-drop opener: single short shouted line) but COLD marking governs numeral/close. Verified first line: "WHY DIDN'T YOU WEAR YOUR EMERALD BRACELET?"

p3c2.title: Chapter II

p3c3.caption: STA W-III · 4,162 words · FIG OFFICE
p3c3.contentRationale: The bargain stated honestly in Wynand's office (Stoneridge commission for herself — 'I have saved you time and lies'; 'the person before last'); statue theme vs her theme ('exaltation' / 'suffering'); restaurant vivisection of Keating (Michelangelo/Palladio/Wren, Holcombe goad, salad plate swept off); night admission to the locked gallery no outsider ever entered.
p3c3.notes: SPLIT = two figures across the desk. Desk-line vignette + contract slip + 3 ascending ticks (the three dead masters). Correction applied: the 'price of one / bargain' is Keating's buildings, not Stoneridge; the goad is the Holcombe threat.

p3c4.caption: STA W-IV · 3,171 words · FIG SEA
p3c4.contentRationale: Sunset boarding of the yacht whose name answers 'You don't run things around here' ('It's an answer'); dinner debate on love as reverence/worship/glory/upward glance vs pity; mutual skyline/skyscraper credo ('Buildings … Skyscrapers'); proposal by restraint ('to be conventional is the only abnormality possible'); her resistance is the remembered Banner caption 'Are you happy, Mr. Superman?' under Roark's photograph.
p3c4.notes: STRATA = green-sky sea bands + fire-trace. White bow wedge + painted 'I Do' name + rail stanchions. Bookended by p3c9 (vow → reckoning). Verified: 'gold letters—I Do—on the delicate white bow'.

p3c5.caption: STA W-V · 7,428 words · FIG STONERIDGE
p3c5.contentRationale: Keating takes Stoneridge ('I want it all!') + check 'for two hundred and fifty thousand dollars'; Wynand bans Dominique's name/picture from all his papers ('henceforward any mention…'); her Clayton, Ohio detour — night stoop across from Roark's excavation, room questionnaire, refused plea, clinging sheet snatched/crumpled/flung, headlight widening, military-salute farewell; Toohey binds Scarret ('get rid of Jimmy Kearns').
p3c5.notes: CLIMAX: solid Gilt numeral + hearth as work-light glare. Derrick/girder + headlight orb; check-slip second detail. No drop-cap letterform (quote-led no-drop opener). Verified: 'WHAT'S THE MATTER? DON'T I GET STONERIDGE?'

p3c6.caption: STA W-VI · 4,527 words · FIG MUSKRAT
p3c6.contentRationale: Lois Cook's salon: Ike reads his muskrat play ('CHUCK: AND WHY NOT A MUSKRAT?'), Fougler hooks the script with his cane — 'This is a great play' / 'Because I say so' / 'I think it smells. That is why it's great'; Toohey's leveling doctrine ('you're just as great as Ibsen'), dentist autobiography, 'One Small Voice' / 'Grandeur of the Little' (Bassett Brush plant by Augustus 'Gus' Webb); Keating surrenders Stoneridge to Neil Dumont and Bennett; Francon retires; 'Stoneridge was the last contract signed by the firm of Francon & Keating.'
p3c6.notes: COLD: Bronze stroke numeral + Bronze cap/end-mark. Cane-hook + dragged script; inverted star second detail. Corrections applied: 'Neil Dumont and Bennett' (not 'Dumont & Bennett'); Augustus Webb (Gus in salon); partner firm 'Peter Keating & Cornelius Dumont'.

p3c7.caption: STA W-VII · 4,173 words · FIG TRAIN
p3c7.contentRationale: Reno-return platform reunion ('I love you … as if the words were a statement of pain') then her demand for the most ostentatious public wedding: Noyes-Belmont, 600, floodlights, black dress + jasmine on black wrist band, judge's slow words, his private 'act of pure religion', assembly-belt receiving line; every Wynand paper barred ('two lines on page eighteen'); wedding night reveals the glass cage demolished into 'a solid vault without a single window'; hate-mail hamper ('Thousands'), rival papers run the nude statue, Toohey plants Layton money by proxy — 'I'd give my life for the New York Banner.'
p3c7.notes: SINGLE-LO = twin rails + sleepers. Platform pair + jasmine-on-black-band second detail. Correction applied: 'page eighteen' (words). Verified first line: 'WHEN DOMINIQUE STEPPED OFF THE TRAIN IN NEW YORK…'.

p3c7.readingTreatment: Shared calm body; hamper letters as inset clippings; vault paragraph gets stone-rule break; Gilt ◆ + END · FIG TRAIN

p3c8.caption: STA W-VIII · 4,041 words · FIG PENTHOUSE
p3c8.contentRationale: Two weeks sealed in the penthouse ('anchored in space, not an island, but a planet'); Sally Brent smuggles the forbidden Dominique story and is fired ('To hell with her public'), proof wad hurled at Dominique's face; the raindrop-diamond necklace ('diamonds without visible settings … like drops of water fallen at random'; 'I was an alchemist'); the FIRE THE BITCH cablegram on her mirror; spring theater night ('No Skin Off Your Nose') detonates ('Shut up! … Shut up, God damn you!') and ends in mutual treason confession ('We've committed the same treason somewhere').
p3c8.notes: DRILL = glass-cage mullions. Emberlight diamond rhomb + cablegram-slip second detail. Corrections applied: full 'Shut up!' scream quote; 'holding the frame of the window' (no grip/midnight — 'midnight' absent from chapter); sunflower is on Sally Brent's shoulder.

p3c9.caption: STA W-IX · 3,372 words · FIG YACHT
p3c9.contentRationale: Yacht-deck reckoning: credo of power and breaking men ('The man I couldn't break would destroy me'; 'I hate the impossible conception you love so passionately'); fall parapet scene — lighted-window shafts, Cord Building threads, 'There's no Wynand Building in New York … the final symbol', Hell's Kitchen rooftop memory; her plea ('Gail, fire Ellsworth Toohey'; tank vs 'corrosive gas') refused — 'It's an ultimatum'; final tenderness ('my ego and my naked need'), her fear ('Of what I'm doing to you'), and the cablegram crumpled over the wastebasket.
p3c9.notes: CLIMAX: solid Gilt numeral + hearth as deck-rail dusk line. Rail/bow + 'I Do' bookend to p3c4; crumpled-cablegram polygon second detail (paper destroyed twice). Verified: 'She crumpled it, her fingers twisting slowly in a grinding motion against her palm.'
